summary: Several studies have directly applied graph neural networks to the task of hate speech detection. El-Sayed et al. (2022) [V0097] used message passing over relational graphs on the ToxiBench dataset, achieving an AUROC of 0.93. Gupta et al. (2024) [V0099] employed a similar approach on ProtMap, reporting an accuracy of 0.72. Haddad et al. (2025) [V0100] applied message passing over relational graphs to FireScope for hate speech detection, obtaining a test MAE of 0.79. Fischer et al. (2023) [V0098] also used message passing over relational graphs on GridWatch, achieving an F1 score of 0.65. Additionally, Brennan et al. (2018) [V0117], while not using graph neural networks, applied representation learning with paired positive and negative examples on ToxiBench, achieving an F1 score of 0.78, which serves as a relevant baseline.
